subject: [RFC PATCH 03/57] mm/collapse: add collapse.h for the shared collapse state

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the LLM-generated text does not read naturally due to its writing style, which deviates from the author's usual tone and phrasing, and suggested instructing the model to preserve the original tone and focus on grammar corrections.
reviews.raw_body:
It doesn't read the way you would usually write. In a bad way.

E.g., "Your shape", "has to open the series"

Consider telling the LLM to not change your writing style and focus only on
fixing grammar.

Otherwise it will be very load bearing to read and we'll be sorry to have to
gently push back against that.


Imagine I would instead have written the following:

The text does not read the way you would normally write, and the difference is
noticeable in a way that makes it feel less natural.

For example, phrases such as \u201cYour shape\u201d and \u201chas to open the series\u201d do not
sound consistent with your usual writing style.

It may be worth instructing the LLM to preserve your original tone and phrasing
as much as possible, and to focus only on correcting grammar and obvious
language issues.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Lorenzo requested the patch be broken down into a smaller initial series, citing his own experience with the scalable CoW series as an example of how to lay foundations for future work.

Reviewer Lorenzo (ARM) expressed frustration with the large number of automated responses, suggesting that Kiryl Shutsemau should write his own replies instead of relying on AI-generated text.
reviews.raw_body:
Please don't respin this as a 57 patch series.

You need to break this into a smaller initial series that lays some
foundations.

Cf. what I've done with scalable CoW series as an example.

---

Even this reads as AI-generated... Consider writing the replies yourself
please.

You've generated a ton of work here and the AI-style giant replies just
create more.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the patch series was not intended to be a step-by-step guide, but rather a demonstration of the final form. They plan to restructure the patchset by moving cleanups and refactoring to the front and submitting them in smaller chunks.
reviews.raw_body:
I didn't plan to.

The goal of this RFC was to show the final form I want to reach.

I will move cleanups and refactoring to the front of the patchset and
submit in small self-contained chunks while keeping the rest working in
a private branch.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo expressed frustration with the use of large blocks of text in replies, specifically mentioning that LLM-generated responses can be difficult to parse and overwhelming to review. He suggested that writing responses manually would help avoid this issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Sorry that wasn't intended as personal. Text is a bad medium.

What I meant to say is I agree with David re: the use of LLMs in replies, it's
not helpful in that it leads to the usual issue of very large blocks of texts
that are difficult to parse.

So put in a clearer way - I meant to say that writing them yourself would avoid
this issue.

My experience is that the series as a whole is overwhelming to review in its
current form, and adding more material to get through this way makes it more
difficult.

Hopefully this clears up what I was trying to say... :)

2026-08-24.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of folio_put() to handle a race condition when shrinking memory. It ensures that even if there's a concurrent refcount decrease, the partially_mapped state will be properly cleaned up and stats updated.
